bounds.domain: The adapter case covers one key, two single-write callers, one external reset, one reopened reader and one serialized write transaction. It starts with absence or one legacy draft and uses distinct opaque byte values, including a revisioned empty row. The controller case covers one send, one consume, one optional fresh reader and one optional non-dispatch release. It uses at most two keys and three revisions per key.
bounds.assumptions: IndexedDB serializes readwrite transactions and exposes a staged put on commit. Revisions are fresh. Absence and reset tombstones share the draft-layer null value. A dispatched raw-slot write does not receive the caller's signal. The controller case assumes successful storage receipts, a host that honors the restore predicate, and a hold that claims the shared queue first in the simultaneous call case.
bounds.limitations: The mandatory Chromium hook runs the 12 adapter groups and three mixed controller groups. The direct command bun run --cwd packages/ui test:browser-document-store runs Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, or its selected engines. The controller case excludes concurrent external writes, same-key peer autosave, restore rejection, other terminal outcomes and repeated attempts. The adapter case excludes arbitrary external byte restoration, Web Locks editing, version upgrades and disk eviction. Generated traces are not replayed.

assumptions: Weak fairness of each dispatched writer's eligible adapter and transaction steps. A staged write eventually commits or fails. A checked writer can proceed when the store has released the transaction.
No fairness. A dispatched operation can remain stalled if the browser never advances an eligible storage step.
